name: Jay Obernolte

statements.quote: AI is poised to become a foundational driver of innovation worldwide. From serving as a personal assistant to generating computer code to advancing the frontiers of human science, the scope and impact of AI continues to expand at an extraordinary pace. It is critical that Congress does its job in enacting an appropriate federal framework for this burgeoning new technology. It is also imperative that this framework maintains the position of the United States as the leading force in the development and deployment of worldwide AI.
statements.venue: Opening statement at House Science Committee hearing 'Advancing America's AI Action Plan'

statements.quote: The FRONTIER Act focuses oversight on the largest developers and most advanced models, requiring transparency, independent evaluation, and timely reporting of serious safety incidents. This legislation will protect Americans from catastrophic risk, provide developers with clear rules of the road, and ensure the United States remains the global leader in AI.
statements.venue: Press release introducing the FRONTIER Act

statements.quote: Artificial intelligence is advancing rapidly, which is why Congress must take a thoughtful and bipartisan approach to regulating this critical technology
statements.venue: Press release on Great American AI Act discussion draft

statements.quote: Well, there's already product liability, it's just not clear where that liability lies. It's not clear, when harm occurs, who is liable. Is it the people that deployed the model, is it the people that modified the model, is it the people that — the developers that created the model, is it the people that created the data that the model was trained [on]? So, that is very unclear and certainly should be clarified.
statements.venue: Fox News Channel 'America's Newsroom' interview (via Breitbart)

statements.quote: But that's not job one. Job one is to require companies to have safety plans and to follow those safety plans, and that's not — that's what we don't have right now.
statements.venue: Fox News Channel 'America's Newsroom' interview (via Breitbart)

statements.quote: We certainly don't want to let industry write the rules for governing itself.
statements.venue: Fox News 'America's Newsroom' interview (Fox News live updates)

statements.quote: The sooner we can act, the better. [...] So, God forbid we have a Chernobyl moment at some point here that really causes harm to people and focuses the public's attention on AI in a way that we hope it will never be.
statements.venue: Remarks to reporters on Capitol Hill (Fox News)

statements.quote: I think the president was talking about the dangers of over-regulation, and that's something I very much agree with him on.
statements.venue: Response to Fox News Digital on Trump's AI comments

statements.quote: I think the need for action is urgent. We have been saying this for the last year and a half.
statements.venue: CNN interview

statements.quote: Were going to be continuing to monitor AI as it matures, and create a framework that is flexible enough to change and capture these new trends when come online
statements.venue: Remarks at INCOMPAS Policy Summit (Broadband Breakfast)

statements.quote: If you’re going to do a comprehensive job at implementing a federal regulatory framework, it’s going to be detailed
statements.venue: Comments reported by Punchbowl News on forthcoming AI bill

statements.quote: This legislation brings together experts and lawmakers to develop clear, actionable recommendations to strengthen our workforce, support American workers, and ensure the United States continues to lead the world in innovation.
statements.venue: Statement on Economy of the Future Commission Act (Ripon Advance)

statements.quote: AI is reshaping our economy and opening doors to innovation and prosperity that were unimaginable just a few years ago. The potential benefits to our country are enormous, but we will only realize them if Congress establishes a thoughtful and balanced policy framework for AI.
statements.venue: Republican Policy Committee / AEI 'Meet the Experts' event statement

statements.quote: As AI systems grow more powerful, the infrastructure required to support them must evolve just as quickly. [...] Liquid cooling is a critical innovation that will reduce energy use, improve efficiency, and ensure the United States remains at the forefront of AI development. By driving federal adoption, we can set the pace for the private sector and create a unified approach that strengthens America's AI ecosystem.
statements.venue: Press release on Liquid Cooling for AI Act

statements.quote: Congress needs to clarify where the interstate commerce guardrails are and where states are free to be the laboratories of democracy that they always have been
statements.venue: Remarks at Fisher Phillips AI Conference

statements.quote: The most destructive thing is if there’s fear out there that every few years as the winds of political fortune shift, the rules governing the use of AI completely change
statements.venue: House Energy and Commerce hearing on state AI law moratorium (CalMatters)

statements.quote: If you go through those negative outcomes, we already have laws that make the malicious use of AI illegal. [...] They don’t specifically say AI. For example, the use of AI to steal someone’s money is already illegal. We don’t need to pass a law to do that.
statements.venue: Georgetown Center for Digital Ethics event (The Hoya)

statements.quote: I think it’s very short-sighted of them, because they did this out of the fear and belief that the use of AI will result in fewer jobs for scriptwriters
statements.venue: Georgetown Center for Digital Ethics event (The Hoya)

statements.quote: While there are many unknowns about artificial intelligence, I believe AI has the potential to create a rising wave of productivity, prosperity, and empowerment in America.
statements.venue: X post

statements.quote: But you raise an interesting counterpoint, which is that there’s fear of industry capture, where sometimes, when the federal government establishes regulation over an industry, industry seeks to turn that into a barrier to entry for smaller competitors.
statements.venue: Fast Company interview

statements.quote: We must also ensure that our academic institutions continue to play an active role in research and development of AI, and that the transparent system of publication and peer review that has enabled its success thus far is not replaced with an opaque system where cutting-edge research is only performed by corporations. This is why I believe is it critically important that we establish a National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource (NAIRR) as a shared national research infrastructure to ensure researchers have access to the tools needed to test, develop, and create new AI-backed technologies.
statements.venue: Opening statement at House Science Committee joint subcommittee hearing on AI risk management
